explanation: Read the current top, right, bottom and left boundaries, then move each boundary inward. Guard the last row and column so the center is never repeated.
timeComplexity: O(n²) time for an n by n matrix. Account for each layer’s actual loops and, in Python, its full matrix transpositions.
spaceComplexity: O(n²) output space and O(1) other space. Boundary indices are constant-sized; the output holds every matrix entry. Python additionally builds full transposed matrices.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract; EPI problem attribution remains in the collection.
correctness: The four boundaries enclose exactly the unvisited rectangle. Reading its top, right, bottom and left edges visits the outer ring in clockwise order. Moving each boundary inward removes only visited cells. The final-row and final-column guards prevent overlap when a ring collapses. Repeating the invariant visits every cell once in spiral order.
walkthrough: For [[21, 22, 23], [31, 32, 33], [41, 42, 43]], read the top row 21, 22, 23; the right edge 33, 43; the bottom edge backward 42, 41; and the left edge upward 31. Only center 32 remains. Return [21, 22, 23, 33, 43, 42, 41, 31, 32]. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: An empty square produces no output.
A 1 by 1 square emits its center once.
Odd-sized matrices have a final center; even-sized matrices finish with a ring and no repeated cells.
